chunks: My father and Muhammad b. al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on them both) narrated to us. They said: Sa'd b. 'Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. 'Isa, from Musa b. al-Qasim al-Bajali, from Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Sama'a, from 'Abdullah b. Muskan, from al-Hakam b. al-Salt, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Take hold of the belt of this bald man - meaning 'Ali - for indeed he is the Greatest Truthful One (al-Siddiq al-Akbar), and he is the Distinguisher (al-Faruq) who distinguishes between truth and falsehood. Whoever loves him, Allah will guide him; whoever hates him, Allah will hate him; and whoever strays from him, Allah will destroy him. From him are the two descendants of my nation - al-Hasan and al-Husayn - and they are my two sons. From al-Husayn are the Imams of guidance: Allah gave them my knowledge and my understanding. So align yourselves with them, and do not take intimate allies from besides them, or else the anger of your Lord will descend upon you; and whoever has the anger of his Lord descend upon him, he will surely perish - and the life of this world is nothing but a deceptive enjoyment.

key_terms.أَئِمَّةُ هُدَاةٍ: Imams of guidance, the divinely appointed leaders
key_terms.الصِّدِّيقُ الْأَكْبَرُ: The Greatest Truthful One, a title of Ali
key_terms.الْأَنْزَعِ: The bald/removed one, a distinctive epithet
key_terms.الْفَارُوقُ: The Distinguisher between truth and falsehood
key_terms.حُجْزَةِ: Belt/waistband, metaphor for clinging to someone
key_terms.وَلِيجَةً: Intimate allies/confidants taken besides rightful leaders

ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Muhammad say about holding fast to Ali and the Imams from Husayn's lineage?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (s) instructs his followers to hold fast to 'Ali, calling him the Greatest Truthful One and the Distinguisher between truth and falsehood, declaring that love or hatred of 'Ali determines divine guidance or punishment. He then identifies al-Hasan and al-Husayn as his own sons and descendants, and announces that the Imams of guidance descend from al-Husayn, having been given the Prophet's knowledge and understanding. The hadith concludes with a Quranic warning against taking protectors besides the Imams, lest divine anger descend. This tradition was delivered in the context of establishing the line of Imamate through the Prophet's direct family, a central teaching of Shi'a Islam.
